svg.aria-label: Code keeps the run on track; agents make the calls. One /bkit-build run in three rows. Agents: models, each one fresh, making the judgement calls. Three each build one group of tasks and one reviews the diff for bugs and security; each starts on a brief of a few KB and hands over before 160 thousand tokens, takes its brief from the engine and hands back a log and a verdict. Engine: bkit commands, plain code with the same answer every time, covered by 5,800+ tests. context brief: cuts each group's part out of the plan; tests red: proves each new test fails before its code exists; steps gate: stops a step missing its verdict or files; counters route: counts fix rounds, stops at the limit; status resume: where a stopped run picks up, on any tool; ledgers append: writes lessons and decisions as checked rows; workflows summary: writes the run's verdict, reasons and next command. Your repo: the plain files the engine reads and writes: the whole plan, run state, step logs, 4 ledgers and run stats. Build agents never get the whole plan: the engine reads it and hands each one only its part. What the split gets you: steps that can't be faked, because a step missing its verdict or files can't finish, whatever the agent says; the same answer every time, on every tool; and, as a bonus, fewer tokens, because no model turn is spent on bookkeeping and no agent carries a long history.
